Mr. German began putting his savings from teaching to working his own farm. Although a bachelor for a long time, he secured his higher education from the University of Missouri. He taught school until he was twenty-six, when the Civil War interrupted his teaching.

In 1874 Mr. German came to Texas. Although a bachelor for some years, he had a former pupil and assistant teacher, Eliza Paxton, a Kentuckian by birth, the daughter of Samuel S. Paxton, who had moved his family to Missouri and was well known as a Kentucky pioneer farmer. He married Miss Eliza Paxton in 1874. They had no children; both Sam Houston and Samuel L. Clements. She introduced both Sam Houston and Samuel L. Clemens. She became a class[?] under R. F. Taylor, and also became a game warden under Ben Wyatt. I was also a deputy sheriff under John A. Phillips in Grayson County, Oklahoma.
